sections.history: Tirukkadaiyur, about 21 km east of Mayiladuthurai near the old coastal town of Tharangambadi, is an ancient Shaiva site sung in the seventh-century Tevaram. The present masonry temple was raised during the Chola period, from around the ninth century, and greatly enlarged under the Thanjavur Nayaks, who added its tall towers and spacious halls. Its eastern gopuram rises eleven storeys, and the complex spreads across five courtyards — a scale that matches its standing as both a Tevaram sthalam and an Ashta Veerattanam shrine.
sections.architecture: The temple is a large Dravidian complex of concentric prakaras, pillared mandapas and several gateway towers, the eastern one among the tallest in the region. The sanctum enshrines the lingam of Amritaghateswarar; a separate and much-visited shrine houses the goddess Abirami, and another honours Markandeya. The form of Shiva as Kalasamharamurti — foot raised against Yama — is a focus of worship, and devotees look for the marks said to have been left on the lingam by the god of death's noose.
sections.legends: The great legend of Tirukkadaiyur is that of Markandeya. Granted a brilliant but short life, the boy was a fervent devotee of Shiva; when Yama came on his appointed last day and cast his noose, the boy clung to the lingam, and the noose fell around the stone itself. Shiva burst forth and struck down Yama to protect his devotee, conquering death and earning the name Kalasamharamurti — later restoring Yama so that the order of the world could continue. The place name is also linked to a pot (ghata) of the nectar of immortality, from which the lord takes the name Amritaghateswarar.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the full Shaiva calendar, with Maha Shivaratri and the festival of Kalasamharamurti observed with particular grandeur. Above all, Tirukkadaiyur is the favoured site for Sashtiabdhapoorthi and Sadabhishekam — the 60th- and 80th-birthday ceremonies at which couples renew their vows and pray for long life — and families travel here from across Tamil Nadu and beyond to perform them.
sections.experience: For many visitors Tirukkadaiyur is a once-in-a-lifetime journey tied to a milestone birthday, and the temple hums with family ceremonies alongside daily worship. The towering gopurams, the Abirami shrine fragrant with devotion, and the deep association with victory over death give the place an atmosphere at once festive and profoundly reassuring.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirukkadaiyur is about 21 km east of Mayiladuthurai and close to the coastal town of Tharangambadi (Tranquebar) in Mayiladuthurai district; the nearest rail heads are Mayiladuthurai and Sirkazhi, with regular buses and taxis to the temple town.
